summary: An excerpt from a fiction book (Book 10, part 50) in which Greg, a Google employee, confronts a pudgy, pale, curly-haired man who claims to work for a DC firm employed by Google. Greg threatens to go to the press, but the man counters with offers of money, a team role, and political work, which Greg rejects as an attempt to smear candidates. The scene mixes tense confrontation with odd domestic details like rinsing coffee beans.
one_line: Greg, a Google employee, refuses a mysterious DC operative's offer to join a team and smear political candidates, threatening to go to the press.
key_facts: Greg is confronted by a man who says he works for a DC firm in Google's employ, described as the inventors of swiftboating.
The man tells Greg, "You're a Googler. You're part of the family."
Greg says, "I'll go to the press," and claims he has written everything up.
The man says the Chronicle would try to find a confirming source and "They won't find it."
The man says his work is "the win-win business" and that he is "very good at it."
The man tells Greg to rinse the beans first because it "takes some of the bitterness out and brings up the oils."
The man hangs his jacket over a kitchen chair, rolls up his cuffs, and slips a cheap digital watch into his pocket.
The man is described as a little pudgy, very pale, and in need of a haircut with unruly curls at his neck.
The man says, "We're drafting a team for Building 49," and Greg replies, "There is no building 49."
The man says the team will own googlecleaner, noting that Maya's code "clobbers the whole farm" every time someone runs it.
The man offers Greg money, good work, smart colleagues, and "A chance to participate in the political life of your country."
Greg responds with a bitter laugh and says, "If you think I'm going to help you smear political candidates in exchange for favors, you're even crazier than I thought."
